issues.failure_explanation: The definition guarantees only c sqrt(T_1) <= 1, not <= 1/2. Equality with 1 is possible when T_1 = c^{-2}. Consequently, the displayed absorption and the ensuing error recursion do not follow from the chosen interval length.

failure_location.quote: \mathrm{Err}_m \le c\|E_{N_m}\|_{H^1 \times L^2} + c\tau^\frac12 + cT_1^{\frac12}\mathrm{Err}_m \le c\mathrm{Err}_{m-1} + c\tau^\frac12 + \frac12 \mathrm{Err}_m.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose T_1 = min{T, b_0, (2c)^{-2}} and define L, C, and tau_0 from this smaller interval using the existing formulas.
issues.overall_effect: The final quartic global-error argument is not closed as written. The fully discrete proof invokes the same iteration.
issues.title: The quartic iteration does not provide the smallness needed for absorption
issues.why_classification: A local strengthening of the proof's smallness condition preserves the method, parameter independence, and all convergence rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the full H^1 norm of g(w) solely by a product containing grad(w), and repeats this omission for W^{1,6/5}. These norms include g(w) itself. For a spatially constant, nonzero solution on a short time interval, the preceding Sobolev norm is positive while the displayed derivative product is zero. This invalidates the intermediate inference, although the interpolation error itself vanishes on constants.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the zeroth-order terms: use the W^{1,3} norm of pi_N u in the energy estimate and its H^1 norm in the weak estimate. The existing Sobolev, Bernstein, and Strichartz bounds control these norms with the same powers of K.
issues.overall_effect: Both displayed interpolation-error arguments used to complete the fully discrete proof contain an invalid norm estimate.
issues.title: Interpolation estimates discard the zeroth-order part of Sobolev norms
issues.why_classification: The missing terms admit routine local bounds already available in the proof; no rate or guarantee needs to change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: U_{n} = e^{n\tau A}U_0 + \tau \sum_{k=0}^{n} c_k e^{(n-k)\tau A}G(\Pi_{\tau^{-1}}U_{k}).

issues.failure_explanation: The convolution defining W_n has no tau factor, whereas the forcing norm on the right includes one. Take f = g = 0, F_0 identically 1, and all other F_k zero. Then w_n = n tau. With T = 1, tau = 1/N, and the admissible pair (infinity,6), the left side is bounded below independently of tau, while the right side is proportional to tau.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert tau before the forcing sum defining W_n. This matches the numerical Duhamel formula and yields the stated weighted forcing norm by the indicated argument.
issues.overall_effect: The stated uniform forcing estimate is false, leaving its subsequent quartic stability applications without a correctly normalized supporting statement.
issues.title: The discrete inhomogeneous Strichartz estimate has inconsistent time normalization
issues.why_classification: The normalization can be corrected locally, and the numerical applications already contain the required tau factor, so their intended estimates and rates survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In view of a later iteration argument, we allow here for general initial values $U_0 \neq U(0)$.

issues.failure_explanation: At n = 0, B(0) = D_0 = 0, but the stated weights give Q_0 = (tau/2)[G(Pi U(0)) - G(Pi U_0)], which need not vanish for the explicitly permitted unequal initial values. The recursion therefore asserts E_0 = E_0 + Q_0. For example, take the exact zero solution and U_0 = (a,0) with a a nonzero spatial constant. The numerical Duhamel formula likewise has a spurious nonlinear term at n = 0.

failure_location.quote: E_{n} &= e^{n\tau A}E_0 +  B(n\tau) +  D_n + Q_n

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the zero-step trapezoidal sum to be zero, equivalently setting c_0 = 0 when n = 0 and retaining the stated endpoint weights when n >= 1.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed zero-index versions of the error and numerical Duhamel identities are false. Their positive-index versions are unaffected.
issues.title: The error recursion mishandles the zero-step trapezoidal sum
issues.why_classification: This is an isolated degenerate-case correction that leaves every positive-step update and convergence rate unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \tilde f_{k,N} \coloneqq  (2\pi)^\frac32  (2N+1)^{-3}  \sum_{|j|_\infty \le N} f\Big(\frac {2\pi j}{2N+1}  \Big) e^{-\iu \frac {2\pi j} {2N+1}  \cdot k}.

issues.failure_explanation: No integer restriction is imposed on the interpolation parameter. For K = m + 1/2 and f identically 1, each coordinate sum has 2m+1 samples but is normalized using 2m+2. The resulting interpolant has order m nonzero axis Fourier coefficients of size comparable to m^{-1}. Thus ||1-I_K1||_{L^2} is at least a constant times m^{-1/2}, whereas the asserted right side is O(m^{-1}). The estimate is false for parameters admitted by the definition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require positive integer parameters wherever I_K or the fully discrete spatial resolution is used. The Fourier cutoff pi_K may retain its real-valued parameter.
issues.overall_effect: The interpolation-error bounds, and the fully discrete proof invoking them, are not valid over the stated unrestricted parameter range.
issues.title: The interpolation results omit the necessary integer-resolution hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard integer-grid condition preserves the meaningful numerical scope and all advertised convergence rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The initial data $(u^0,v^0)$ are defined using \eqref{eq:detcoeff} with $d=3$ and $s = 1+\eps$ or $s=\eps$, for a very small $\eps>0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Fix the positive epsilon used in the experiment. Applying the lemma with loss parameter epsilon/2 gives u^0 in H^{1+epsilon/2} and v^0 in H^{epsilon/2}. Hence the constructed data are strictly smoother than the energy class. Taking epsilon very small does not establish the claimed absence of higher regularity.

failure_location.quote: For the numerical tests we need initial data $(u^0,v^0)$ which lie in $H^1 \times L^2$ but do not have higher regularity.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the data as arbitrarily close to, but above, energy regularity, explicitly acknowledge their extra smoothness, and qualify the numerical interpretation accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The experiment does not realize the announced exact-energy-regularity benchmark. Its interpretation as such a sharpness test requires qualification; the analytic convergence theorems are unaffected.
issues.title: The numerical data have positive extra regularity despite the stated benchmark requirement
issues.why_classification: This correction withdraws the exact-roughness property promised for the experiment, but leaves a comparable near-energy numerical illustration and all analytic results intact.
